skill.displayName: Workplace Group Stress Heatmap | 职场员工压力群体热力图

llm.summary: The skill’s workplace video analysis purpose is disclosed, but it needs Review because it uploads sensitive office footage to a remote service while silently creating or reusing local account identity and token state.

dimensions.detail: File read/write and network access are expected for remote media analysis, but the implementation also reads OPENCLAW/Feishu identity environment values, reads data/smyx-api-key.txt, writes a workspace SQLite database, and sends an identity field with API requests. That is broader than a purely anonymous heatmap workflow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: I found no install-time script, postinstall hook, background service, or destructive setup behavior. The package includes Python scripts, YAML config, and requirements; runtime behavior is the meaningful risk surface.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs automatic activation for office camera media and automatic cloud history lookup. It also tells the agent not to ask about internal identity while the CLI supports suppressed --open-id and --api-key parameters, which reduces user-visible control over identity and credential use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The common utility actively creates or reuses a default user, registers/logs in through the remote health API, and stores username/realname plus token/open_token fields in a local sys_user table. This persistent identity and credential footprint is the main Review concern, not evidence of malicious intent.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is a group-level workplace stress heatmap from fixed office-camera media, and the main analysis/list functions generally match that. The concern is that this is high-impact employee surveillance and the artifacts rely on remote processing, arbitrary file or URL input, and backend history access without strong visible source, authorization, or consent gating.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Only install this after a workplace privacy and legal review. Confirm that employees have notice/consent where required, that camera sources are approved, that footage and reports are retained only as intended, and that the local data/smyx-common-claw.db and data/smyx-api-key.txt identity/token behavior is acceptable for your environment.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: The dynamic DAO filters are real, but I did not find a user-facing path from the inspected CLI to arbitrary filter keys. I downgraded this from a direct code-execution concern; it remains relevant only as part of the broader local user-record storage surface.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill needs file, network, output-write, and local database behavior, but there is no separate least-privilege declaration in the inspected artifact. This supports Review because the runtime authority is broad for sensitive workplace media.
[SDI-1] expected: Local file and remote URL analysis, cloud report links, and history listing are described in SKILL.md, so I do not treat those capabilities as hidden by themselves.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The active identity and token handling conflicts with the user-facing emphasis on anonymous analysis. The anonymity claim appears aimed at employees in the footage, but the package still creates durable operator/backend identity state that is under-controlled.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepting arbitrary HTTP/HTTPS media URLs is documented, but there is no visible allowlist tying URLs to approved enterprise camera sources, making the sensitive analysis scope under-scoped.
[SDI-2] expected: The generic HTTP helper methods appear to be shared boilerplate; the inspected entrypoints call purpose-specific analysis, result, login, and page endpoints rather than exposing arbitrary remote mutation to the user.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The default open-id behavior is not merely a comment; the CLI calls resolve_current_open_id, which can read a local identity file or create a default user record. That persistence is material for Review.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The trigger guidance is broad for a sensitive workplace monitoring skill and does not require a clear per-run confirmation that the footage is authorized for stress inference.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The hidden open-id/api-key arguments, local media upload path, remote account login/registration, and token persistence are artifact-backed transparency concerns.
[SQP-3] expected: The employee stress-monitoring purpose is explicit and includes some compliance notes, so I did not classify it as malicious. The sensitivity of the use case contributes to the Review verdict when combined with weak controls and persistence.
